status_legend.MET: Already delivered and verifiable in this repository today.
status_legend.PARTIAL: Partly delivered; the gap is named and linked to an open question.
status_legend.SPECIFIED: Written down with acceptance criteria, not built. Nothing here counts as built because it is specified.
status_legend.BLOCKED: Cannot proceed until a named input, decision or licence exists.

requirements.req: Every NFL game in scope has an official schedule row (date, kickoff, matchup) before any line is attempted.
requirements.accept: 2026 regular-season rows with kickoff or explicit TBD, each carrying an official nfl.com source URL; count reconciles to the league's published week structure.
requirements.gap: Captured 2026 season schedule exists in data/official/events.json from the 2026-11-02 snapshot; 49 preseason matchups have no official dates and 24 regular-season rows carry TBD times.

requirements.req: A market-price source: opening, mid-week and closing prices for spread, total, moneyline and the player-prop lines used by candidate strategies.
requirements.accept: >=3 seasons of timestamped closing lines for spread/total/ML plus prop lines, with per-update timestamps and bookmaker identity; late-line snapshots no later than a stated pre-kickoff cut-off.
requirements.gap: No price feed exists in the repo and none is reachable from the build environment. The Odds API documents exactly the fields needed and a free tier; a licence decision is required first.

requirements.req: Injury and availability tracking for all 32 clubs, at official cadence, stored as an append-only history rather than a current-state overwrite.
requirements.accept: Weekly ingestion of the official per-club report with practice status and game status per player; history retained per report date so 'who was listed, at what status, on which day' is answerable retroactively; blank game status preserved as blank.
requirements.gap: Collector script specified in this section; not run against a schedule yet. The Week 10, 2026 schema and rows used as the reference fixture are verified.

requirements.req: Depth-chart tracking that identifies when a second-, third- or fourth-string player replaces a starter on offense or defense.
requirements.accept: Per-club depth chart captured weekly from the club's official page with its own 'Updated as of' date; diff between consecutive charts produces a starter-change event per position group; vacancy count (positions with fewer than 3 listed players) computed and stored.
requirements.gap: 49ers page verified as the parse target and shows both the cadence and the vacancy problem; the other 31 clubs and a league-wide endpoint are unverified.

requirements.req: Roster-movement awareness: who is unavailable by league rule, not just by injury designation (IR, PUP, NFI, suspended, commissioner exempt, practice-squad elevations).
requirements.accept: Transaction feed parsed into per-player availability windows, with the rule-derived minimum-miss counts recorded alongside (for example an IR designation carries a four-game minimum and consumes one of eight return designations).
requirements.gap: The rule set is verified from an official NFL article written around the 2022 offseason; the current-year wording and the club transaction endpoint still need confirmation (the nfl.com team transactions path 404s).

requirements.req: Participation and snap-level data for the players whose props are being priced.
requirements.accept: Play-level snap participation and route/target participation per player per game, available before the model's decision cut-off, with a documented latency.
requirements.gap: Officially, Next Gen Stats is published the day AFTER the game; box score and play-by-play update live during the game. So snap-share inputs cannot be modelled same-day from the official league source; the cut-off design must respect that.

requirements.req: A line-origination model that produces an independent number for spread, total and moneyline for every in-scope game, before seeing any market price.
requirements.accept: Deterministic, versioned scoring pipeline (roster-adjusted team ratings -> venue/rest adjustment -> expected total and margin -> key-number-aware spread and total), blind to market prices at generation time, with a written pre-registration for each model version.
requirements.gap: No price data (R-02) and no verified player-value table, so the model can be specified and unit-tested on synthetic fixtures but not trained or tuned on real outcomes yet.

requirements.req: The published line must be expressed with vig, and the no-vig fair probability must be recoverable for every price used as a benchmark.
requirements.accept: Implied probability, overround and devigged probability computed from American prices by the documented formula; a two-sided -110 market resolves to 52.38% break-even, which matches the academic break-even threshold used as a sanity check.
requirements.gap: Formula and unit tests can be written now; applying them to real prices requires R-02.

requirements.req: Signal generation: candidate bet signals derived from the difference between our number and the market's number, not from narrative.
requirements.accept: Each signal is a single deterministic rule over stored fields, with the exact cut-off time, the exact threshold, and no post-hoc edits; every signal row records the price it was taken at.
requirements.gap: Signal rules are written in the strategy catalogue; none can be evaluated until prices land.

requirements.req: Single-bet support (spread, total, moneyline, first-half and team-total variants) with per-market cost and settlement assumptions.
requirements.accept: One stake per game per market; push handled as no-action; settlement from the official league box score, never from a screenshot or an aggregator.
requirements.gap: Settlement source is official and available; the entry prices are not.

requirements.req: Parlay and Same-Game-Parlay construction, priced from our own joint distribution rather than from the operator's boost.
requirements.accept: Priced multi-leg tickets with an explicit correlation assumption per leg pair; a legality/rule check that rejects combinations the operator would void or reprice.
requirements.gap: Operator correlation rules are only partially verified this session; each operator's live rulebook must be read before construction.

requirements.req: Player-prop and prop-combo pricing (rush/reception/anytime-TD/fantasy-score style lines).
requirements.accept: A per-player projection distribution for each prop stat we price, plus the line and price for the same prop at >=2 books.
requirements.gap: Props exist in the vendor's documented market list but only from US and AU bookmakers; prop closing lines historically have far thinner archives than main lines, so backtest length is the binding constraint.

requirements.req: Correlation values for every leg pair used in a parlay, with an honest uncertainty range and a source.
requirements.accept: Pairwise outcome correlation estimated on our own resolved history; where no estimate exists, the pair is priced at the Fréchet-Hoeffding bound consistent with the marginal probabilities and the ticket is flagged 'correlation unverified'.
requirements.gap: Requires >=1 season of our own resolved tickets; no structural rho table can be imported as fact.

requirements.req: Every strategy passes a written gate set before it can be promoted, and fails publicly if it does not.
requirements.accept: Gates G-01..G-18 published with thresholds, applied mechanically, results stored per strategy per evaluation; a strategy that fails any blocking gate is parked, not quietly dropped.
requirements.gap: Gate definitions and the data each gate needs are written in this section; no strategy has a result yet because no evaluation has run.

requirements.req: Luck removed as far as arithmetic allows: results are separated from expected value, and sample size governs every claim.
requirements.accept: For each strategy: number of bets, hit rate, mean edge at entry, closing-line value, standard error, t-statistic, and a block-bootstrap confidence interval; no headline ROI without them, and an explicit statement of what sample size would be needed to detect the claimed edge.
requirements.gap: The required-n table is computed and published here from the stated assumptions; it is arithmetic, not a result.

requirements.req: No look-ahead, ever: at decision time the model may only use fields whose own timestamps precede the cut-off.
requirements.accept: Every input row carries as_of_utc and published_utc; the backtest enforces published_utc <= cut-off; the injury-report fixture is deliberately captured as of the Friday report, not the final lineup.
requirements.gap: Enforcement code specified; needs implementation in the collector's schema.

requirements.req: A leaderboard competition where strategies compete for rewards, scored on skill-oriented metrics rather than raw profit.
requirements.accept: Ranking driven by luck-adjusted value (closing-line edge), calibration, minimum-sample compliance and gate pass rate; raw ROI is displayed but is not the promotion criterion.
requirements.gap: Design complete; no entrants, no ledger, no reward pool decision.

requirements.req: Rewards must not turn the competition itself into unlicensed wagering or an incentive to break the rules.
requirements.accept: Reward pool paid from the owner's operating budget, denominated in infrastructure/credits/recognition, never a share of a stake pool; entry is free; no side bets between entrants; the rules are published and frozen for a season before it starts.
requirements.gap: Owner decision on budget and form of reward is open; legal review of the reward mechanism is open (Q-15).

requirements.req: A dedicated suggestions section where improvements are proposed, costed and ranked, so a human chooses the path before anything is implemented.
requirements.accept: Each suggestion carries the problem it solves, 2-3 real options with cost/effort/risk, a recommendation, and an explicit 'not implemented' state until a decision is recorded.
requirements.gap: The 21 suggestions are published as proposals. None of the ones requiring a decision has been implemented by this session.

requirements.req: A closed list of the questions and information gaps that must be answered before any decision is reasonable.
requirements.accept: Every question states what we have, what we do not have, the cheapest way to find out, and which decisions it blocks; unanswered ones stay OPEN and are named on the executive summary.
requirements.gap: Open questions are published; answers requiring paid feeds, an owner decision or a legal review cannot be produced by an agent.

requirements.req: GitHub Pages site with a clean landing page and category subpages, all findings in readable tables, one source link per row.
requirements.accept: Pages build statically, share one navigation, every table row carries data-source-url, unverified values are blank with a flag, and the build fails the gate if a row lacks a source.
requirements.gap: The NFL-model section satisfies this for its own pages; the pre-existing radio dashboard keeps its own gate.

requirements.req: A Flagged for Review page listing irregularities and unverified items with source links, non-blocking for merge.
requirements.accept: Every anomaly found while building gets an IR- id, an evidence line, the source link, and an effect statement; nothing is deleted to make the list shorter.
requirements.gap: IR-027..IR-040 published for this section; the dashboard's IR-001..IR-026 (including the two merged NFL modules) remain on the root flagged page and are not restated here.

requirements.req: No manual input from the owner is required to complete the build tasks; anything genuinely requiring a human decision is escalated as a proposal, not faked.
requirements.accept: Agent-owned tasks (research, code, build, verify, PR, merge, Pages) completed autonomously; owner-owned items (money, licences, which strategy to fund, jurisdiction) listed in the suggestions and questions pages with no agent-supplied answer.
requirements.gap: Owner-owned items remain open by design.

requirements.req: Coordination with parallel sessions on this repository: claims, non-overlapping scope, conflict log, handover rules.
requirements.accept: COORDINATION.md carries this session's claim with its file scope, checked against the open PR file lists before any edit; the section only adds files.
requirements.gap: Open PRs #18/#25/#41/#43 were inspected on 2026-11-13; this section touches none of their files except a single navigation hunk in index.html.

requirements.req: Jurisdiction, age and eligibility constraints stated with official sources, and a responsible-gambling notice that is not decorative.
requirements.accept: Each regulator statement on the page links to that regulator's own publication; the help line and state resource appear on every page of the section; nothing in the section claims a legal opinion.
requirements.gap: Colorado and New Jersey material is verified; state-by-state age/eligibility and non-US legality were not enumerated this session and are listed as blocking questions rather than asserted.

requirements.req: No league or team content is used in a way that implies official status, and no operator's rules are quoted as if they were universal.
requirements.accept: Every source row carries a tier and a retrieval method; secondary aggregators appear in the registry only as cross-check notes with no value rows.
requirements.gap: Two operator/regulator documents are only snippet-verified (PARTIAL) and are labelled as such on the sources page.

requirements.req: A refresh path that can run without an operator at a keyboard, with provenance preserved (raw response, hash, timestamp, URL).
requirements.accept: A GitHub-Actions-runnable collector that writes compressed raw responses plus a manifest of URL/timestamp/SHA-256, then rebuilds the section; failures leave the previous data in place and produce a flag row instead of a silent blank.
requirements.gap: scripts/fetch_nfl_model_sources.py is provided and syntax-checked, but this session did not run it on a runner, so no fresh official snapshot is claimed for 2026-11-13 beyond the pages fetched interactively above.

requirements.req: Reproducible build and a failing CI check when the section's verification gate fails.
requirements.accept: python3 scripts/build_nfl_model.py regenerates every page byte-identically from data; python3 scripts/verify_nfl_model.py exits non-zero on a sourceless row, a fabricated official claim, a broken internal link, or a missing disclosure.
requirements.gap: Both run green locally; the CI job runs them on pull requests to main.
